pollHours.detail: Wis. Stat. 6.78(1m): "The polls at every election shall be open from 7 a.m. until 8 p.m." 6.78(4): any elector waiting to vote at the time the polls officially close shall be permitted to vote.

registration.mailDeadlineDetail: Registration form with proof of residence must be postmarked no later than October 14, 2026.
registration.onlineDetail: Online registration at MyVote requires a valid Wisconsin DMV driver license or state ID matching DMV records.
registration.inPersonClerkDetail: In the municipal clerk's office until 5:00 p.m. (or close of business, whichever is later) on Friday, October 30, 2026. No registration the Saturday, Sunday or Monday before the election.
registration.electionDayRegistrationDetail: Voters may register at their polling place on Election Day, November 3, 2026, 7:00 a.m.-8:00 p.m.
registration.proofOfResidenceDetail: A Proof of Residence document (with name and current residential address) is always required to register by mail, at the clerk's office, or at the polls; a DMV license/ID used for online registration satisfies it. Paper or electronic copies accepted. Corroborating witnesses no longer allowed. Photo ID is never required to register.
acceptedProofOfResidence: Current and valid State of Wisconsin driver license or state ID card
Any other official identification card or license issued by a Wisconsin governmental body or unit
Employer-issued identification card bearing a photo of the card holder (not a business card)
Real estate tax bill or receipt for the current year or the year preceding the election
Residential lease effective on date of registration (not valid if registering by mail)
Gas, electric, or telephone service statement (utility bill) for a period commencing no earlier than 90 days before registration
University, college, or technical college photo ID ONLY with a fee receipt dated within the last 9 months or if the institution provides a certified housing list to the clerk
Intake document from a residential care facility
Bank or credit union statement, or any credit card statement
Identification card issued by a federally recognized Indian tribe in Wisconsin
Documents from a government agency (e.g., hunting/fishing licenses, vehicle registrations, Social Security/Medicare notices, public school/university correspondence) - WEC lists these as examples
registration.residencyRequirement: Must reside at the address at least 28 days by Election Day.

photoId.detail: An original acceptable photo ID must be shown to vote at the polling place or to cast an in-person absentee ballot; a photocopy is required for absentee by mail (exceptions for military, permanent overseas, confidential, indefinitely confined and care-facility voters, and a non-photo DMV ID for sincere religious objection). WI DOT offers a free state ID for voting.
acceptedIdsUnexpiredOrExpiredAfterLastGe: Wisconsin DOT-issued driver license (even if driving privileges revoked or suspended; with or without star)
Wisconsin DOT-issued identification card (with or without star)
Military ID card issued by a U.S. uniformed service
Identification card issued by a federally recognized Indian tribe in Wisconsin (may be used even if expired before the most recent general election)

Photo ID card from a Wisconsin accredited university or college with issuance date, student signature, and expiration no later than two years after issuance (if expired, must be accompanied by proof of current enrollment)
acceptedIdsMustBeUnexpired: Veteran's photo ID card issued by the Veterans Health Administration (U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs)
Certificate of naturalization issued not earlier than two years before the election
Driving receipt issued by Wisconsin DOT (valid 45 days)
Identification card receipt issued by Wisconsin DOT (valid 45 days)

inPersonAbsentee.label: In-person absentee voting (IPAV / early voting)
inPersonAbsentee.detail: Clerks may offer IPAV starting Tuesday, October 20 (two weeks before Election Day) through Sunday, November 1, 2026. Each municipal clerk sets its own dates, hours and locations; some may not offer additional hours. Photo ID required. Ballot must be voted on site.

absenteeByMail.requestDeadlineDetail: Regular and overseas voters: request must be received by the municipal clerk by 5:00 p.m. Thursday, October 29, 2026 (Wis. Stat. 6.86(1)(b): 5 p.m. on the 5th day preceding the election).
absenteeByMail.hospitalizedVoters: May request between October 27 and 5:00 p.m. November 3, 2026 via appointed agent.
absenteeByMail.returnDeadlineDetail: Ballot must be RECEIVED by the municipal clerk (or delivered to the polling place / central count location) by 8:00 p.m. on Election Day, November 3, 2026. Postmarks do not count.
